etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French pianiste, from Italian pianista. Analyzable as piano +‎ -ist.

definitions.definition: (music) A person who plays the piano, particularly with skill or as part of an orchestra.

quote.citation: 1987, Gordon H Bower, The psychology of learning and motivation: advances in research and theory:
quote.text: Table IV shows that the pianists were significantly better on both motor and perceptual timing than the nonpianists.

quote.citation: 2010 April 19, Ben Ratliff, “A Mischievous Convergence of Past and Present Jazz”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: The pianist was Jason Moran, another Houstonian, for whom the past converges with the present: he sometimes likes to find an unobtrusive sequence inside an old standard and turn it into fresh headlines.

definitions.definition: (WWII) A spy using radio or wireless telegraphy to keep in touch with headquarters during the Second World War.
